svg.text: Local developer experience
running everything locally stops scaling (JVM: four or five
services, not twenty); stub services or point at remote
ones; Telepresence for hybrid; keep investing
Running too many things
need desired state management and self-service;
Kubernetes (OpenShift), managed offerings, FaaS;
serverless-first on a public cloud; do not rush to Kubernetes
End-to-end testing
big scope, slow, flaky, a time sink: limit cross-team tests,
use consumer-driven contracts (Pact), progressive delivery
with automated release remediation (Spinnaker at Netflix),
and keep refining quality feedback cycles (remove tests too)
Global versus local optimisation
three teams chose Oracle, MongoDB and PostgreSQL; REA found
many ways to deploy. Use the irreversible/reversible spectrum
(Fig 5-8), a cross-team technical group, or Monzo-style
published proposals; balance autonomy and consistency
Robustness and resiliency
ask per call: how can it fail, and what do I do? Async
communication, time-outs, circuit breakers, multiple copies,
desired state; document production issues; Release It!
Signs and timing
breaking changes and reporting bite fairly early; ownership
as developer numbers grow; e2e testing creeps up with
cross-team journeys; orphans after long use; rare failures
become common as services multiply
